title: Eleven stars, the sun and the moon
hookLine: young Yusuf dreams they bow to him, and his father Ya'qub tells him to keep it to himself
carry: not every dream is for telling
last: WAIT FOR THE ONE WHO'S COMING BACK.

cards: A boy wakes up and runs to tell his father about a dream. Almost everything we've heard about Ibrahim and Musa, the Qur'an tells in pieces, scattered across many surahs; you gather it up like shells on a beach.

Yusuf's story is different. The Qur'an tells it start to finish, in order, in the surah named for him, and at the start it calls what follows the best of stories. For the next two weeks, we'll walk through it in order.

teach.h: ELEVEN STARS, THE SUN AND MOON.
teach.b: Surah Yusuf, verse four. Yusuf says: my father, I saw eleven stars, and the sun and the moon. I saw them bowing down to me.
The Arabic for star, kawkab, can also mean a planet, and some older translations say eleven planets. Either way, the sky is kneeling to a boy.
Commentators read the eleven stars as his eleven brothers, and the sun and the moon as his father and mother. It will take years, and a whole surah, to come true. Keep it in your pocket.
Now Ya'qub, his father, a prophet himself. He doesn't laugh it off, and he doesn't tell the whole family at dinner.
He says: my son, don't tell your dream to your brothers, or they'll plot against you. Satan is a clear enemy to people. He knows his sons, and the jealousy already simmering.
So his first gift to Yusuf is discretion: some good things are safer kept close for a while.
Then the hope: your Lord will choose you, and teach you the meaning of events, and complete His favor on you, as He completed it on your forefathers, Ibrahim and Ishaq.

There's Ibrahim, from earlier on our path, standing in the family line. The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ gave similar advice in a hadith: a good dream is from Allah, and you should tell it only to someone who loves you.

teach.h: NOT EVERY DREAM IS FOR TELLING.
teach.b: Not every dream is for telling. And not everyone who hears it will be glad.

how: Surah Yusuf is recited and taught as one continuous story, and Muslims who follow the prophetic advice share a good dream only with someone who loves them.

o: a sign in the sky that guided a caravan to Egypt
the boy Yusuf's dream of the sky bowing down to him
the eleven prophets before Yusuf in his family line

games.q: what's inside the dream — tap the pairs.

s: the Qur'an tells Yusuf's story in one surah, in order
Surah Yusuf tells it start to finish, and calls it the best of stories.
Ya'qub told the whole family about Yusuf's dream
he told Yusuf: don't tell your brothers, or they'll plot against you.

games.q: you're Ya'qub. your youngest son runs in: he dreamed eleven stars, the sun and the moon bowed to him. his older brothers are nearby. what do you say?
o: tell your brothers. they'll be proud of you.
my son, don't tell your brothers, or they'll plot against you.
it's only a dream. forget it.
games.why: he tells him to keep it close, because he knows the jealousy already there, and then gives him hope: your Lord will choose you.

practice: Think of something good happening for you right now, a hope, a small win, a plan just starting, the kind of thing you'd normally post or mention at dinner.

Hold it in your mind like a folded note in a pocket, and feel what it's like to keep it just for you: not out of fear, out of care, the way Ya'qub cared for his son. If you pray, you can give thanks for it quietly.

wordCard.voice: Eleven stars. The boy Yusuf's dream: eleven stars, the sun and the moon, bowing to him, and a father who said, keep it to yourself. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic, from Qur'an 12:4: "eleven stars" — kawkab is a star or a planet.

carryVoice: Your line: not every dream is for telling. Ya'qub's first gift to his son was a quiet one. Fifty-five days in.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 2261; Sahih al-Bukhari 7044 (a good dream is from Allah; tell it only to one who loves you)
